title: Cooperatives and not-for-profits
log: 2026-11-04T18:10:11Z recheck: the fresh check agreed with the fix, and it was picked as a spot check
2026-11-05T06:08:56Z claude-code review: approved with the fix (a spot check)

draft.title: Cooperatives and not-for-profits
card: Cooperative
a business owned by its members. The members share the benefits, such as lower prices or a share of the earnings.
Not-for-profit
an organisation that puts any surplus back into its purpose. A surplus is money left over after costs are paid.
A group of farmers might form a cooperative to sell their milk together and share the benefits.
A charity that helps homeless people is a not-for-profit. It may pay its staff, but any surplus goes back into its work.
draft.remember: Cooperatives work for their members. Not-for-profits put any surplus back into their purpose.

a.q: A charity runs a food bank and has money left after paying its costs. What does a not-for-profit do with this surplus?
opts: Puts it back into its purpose
Pays it out to private owners
Gives it to the largest donor
Uses it to buy another business
a.why: A not-for-profit puts any surplus back into its purpose, which here is the food bank. Paying it out to private owners is what the other types of business do, not a not-for-profit.
a.clue: The purpose is the reason the group exists.

b.q: Forty fruit growers in the Riverland, South Australia, own a business that packs and sells their fruit together. They share the benefits. What type of business is it?
opts: A cooperative
A not-for-profit charity
A franchise
A sole trader
b.why: The business is owned by its members, the growers, who share the benefits. That makes it a cooperative. It is not a charity, as it does not exist to put a surplus into a cause.
b.clue: Who owns the business, and who shares the benefits?

a.best: Puts it back into its purpose

problems.detail: Why (a) says paying surplus to private owners is 'what the other types of business do'. That overgeneralises. Cooperatives share earnings with their members rather than private owners, and companies do not always pay out all profit. Suggest: 'Paying it out to owners is what businesses run for profit can do, not a not-for-profit.'
